note: Reference values of agent-sharing-spec.md, section 3. Hex unless a name says b64u or base64.
messages_about: One example of each message of the protocol after hello and the list request: name, box (where it goes; the accept's proof goes inside accept), key (a value of this file), nonce (hex, its own), json (the plain text, UTF-8 with no escape of non-ASCII), plain_length (its padded length), sealed_length and sealed_base64. Each end seals json, padded, with key and nonce and gets sealed_base64, and opens sealed_base64 and gets json, padded. Each end's test also WRITES each entry of write_and_compare from its parsed value with its own JSON writer and compares the bytes with json: Foundation and .NET escape '/', '+' and characters that are not ASCII unless they are told not to. A limit of a text counts Unicode code points (Python's len, the Mac's unicodeScalars, Windows' runes); the sealed size is a second limit. 'send 4000 at the edge' has a text of 4,000 code points whose sealed size is the most that fits; 'send 4000 over the edge' has 4,000 code points too, does not fit sealed, and has no nonce and no sealed bytes: each end refuses to seal it, with the code too_long (refused_with), which covers a text of more than 4,000 code points and a text that does not fit sealed. Each of the two texts also has a character above U+FFFF and a combining mark, so its 4,000 code points are 4,001 units of UTF-16 and 3,999 graphemes. 'send 4001' has 4,001 code points (4,001 units of UTF-16, 4,000 graphemes, as Swift's String.count counts them) and fits sealed: the hub opens it and refuses it with too_long (refused_with), so an end that counts graphemes takes a text that the hub refuses. 'list waiting company' is the answer to list of a device that waits for the owner's code while the fleet has the company's part: company holds the company's name (or null), its logo's value (the first 16 lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of the logo's PNG, or null) and logo128, the large logo's value (made the same way from the large logo's PNG of 128 x 128 pixels, or null), the same fields as a member's list, and nothing else of the fleet (decisions D146 and D149). 'device' is the request of a member's phone (B9): its push token, its build's environment and its seal key for this one link (b64u); its answers are 'device answer' and one 'device refused <code>' for each code. 'read with an act' is an answer to 'read' whose agent's message carries a question that waits for the member (P1's act: its key of 16 hex characters, its kind and state, and options and recommended, null for a question with no options); 'send answers' is a send whose words answer that question, by the act's key (answers): its answers are those of 'send', and a key that is not an act of this member with this agent is unknown.

refused.about: Each end refuses each of these: X25519 of private_key with each of public_keys_of_zeros gives 32 zero bytes (RFC 7748, 6.1), and each of invite_texts is no invite file. invite_texts_taken are the two texts of one invite that are read: the line, and the line with one line feed. too_deep is a message of 33 levels of objects, which the hub refuses as it opens it (32 at most); deep_taken has 32 levels, with brackets inside a string, and opens.

member.about: A ping to a member's phone (B9). The phone gave seal_key in its 'device' request (seal, b64u). payload_json is all that our side and Apple carry: the same open part for every member ping, with no item, no db, no name and no number, and 'sealed', which seal_key opens (nonce, json padded to plain_length, sealed_length). collapse goes beside the payload as Apple's collapse id: one notification for each chat, made with a key that HKDF makes from seal_key (collapse_key_label), and another link's key gives another one for the same agent.
member.forms: The two forms, by their open part. The member form is {"aps":{"alert":{"loc-key":"shared-reply"},"mutable-content":1},"sealed":...}, with no other key (our side may add only aps.sound, with the value "default"; never aps.badge). The owner's form has need and db beside aps, and its aps.alert is {"title":"Needs you"}. A phone tries its link keys on the member form only, and reads what one opens in the member form only: no button, no press, no need, whatever the part holds. It tries the owner's key on the owner's form only, and never a link key.

with_need.about: Two payloads that a company's hub could send to a member's phone, each sealed with seal_key and holding a need, options and a title. member_form: the phone opens it with seal_key, shows no button and sends nothing. owner_form: the owner's form (need and db in the open part, the owner's sealed layout with no pad); the phone tries no link key on it, so nothing of it opens on a member's phone.
